_meta.honesty: Nothing here is recalled or inferred.  Anything that could not be derived empirically is marked "source": "UNVERIFIED" and listed under "unverified".
_meta.method: Every value in this fixture was produced by a Stata display and carries the exact command that produced it.  Each date value is recorded twice: "display", the verbatim locale-dependent string Stata prints, and "iso", the same instant re-displayed through an explicit ISO-8601 picture, which is the unambiguous target for a Python converter.  Calendar-period formats (%tw %tm %tq %th) record the period START and END, derived with Stata's own dofw/dofm/dofq/dofh, and %ty with dofy, which takes a YEAR rather than an offset.  Display strings are captured between "<" and ">" sentinels so that leading and trailing blanks -- which are part of what a numeric format means -- survive macro assignment; the sentinels are stripped when the fixture is written.
_meta.record_delimiter_note: Records are pipe-delimited; variable labels had "|" replaced with "/" before writing.  No display format or date string contains a pipe.

%tC.note: A millisecond count from 01jan1960 that DOES include leap seconds, so it is NOT a fixed-length offset.  See "leap_seconds".

%tc.note: A plain millisecond count from 01jan1960 00:00:00.000, with NO leap seconds.  Fixed-length: a timedelta of 'value' ms added to the epoch is exact.

%td.note: A plain day count from 01jan1960.  Fixed-length: a timedelta of 'value' days added to 1960-01-01 is exact.

%th.note: A CALENDAR half-year index; multiplication does not convert.

%tm.note: A CALENDAR month index.  Months are 28-31 days; multiplication does not convert.

%tq.note: A CALENDAR quarter index; multiplication does not convert.

%tw.note: A CALENDAR week index.  Week 1 of every year starts on 01jan and week 52 absorbs the remaining 8 or 9 days, so weeks are not 7 days apart across a year boundary and multiplication does not convert.

%ty.note: %ty is the YEAR ITSELF.  It is not an offset from 1960 and must not be offset at all.  See "ty_is_the_year_itself".

values.note: dofy() is undefined outside years 0100-9999, so no ISO date could be derived empirically for this %ty value; the value itself IS the year.

jsonio_display_formats.claim_in_plan: jsonio has no option that emits display formats; jsonio.ado:238 gates on inlist("`metaprint'`filenm'", ...)

dashstyle.cmd: jsonio out date close, what(all) filenm(<path>) metaprint(varnames varlabels vallabs labelnames)

metaprint_with_filenm.cmd: jsonio out date close, filenm(<path>) metaprint(varlabels)

jsonio_display_formats.finding: CONFIRMED on all three counts.  (1) jsonio.ado line 238 gates the metadata branch on inlist("`metaprint'`filenm'", ...), which CONCATENATES the two macros, so any non-empty filenm() makes the test unmatchable and metaprint() becomes a no-op -- exactly what dash.ado:1481 does.  (2) The metaprint() keys StataMetaToJSON accepts are ['varlabels', 'varnames', 'vallabs', 'labelnames'] -- none is a display format.  (3) The what(all) payload jsonio actually wrote carries top-level keys ['firstRecordId', 'lastRecordId', 'numberOfRecords', 'numberOfVariables', 'valueLabelNames', 'valueLabels', 'values', 'variableIndices', 'variableIsString', 'variableLabels', 'variableNames'], with no format member.  jsonio therefore cannot emit display formats and dash must carry them itself.

gating_fallthrough.meaning: metaprint() with a filenm() and NO what() produced a payload byte-identical to what(all): after the line 238 test fails, control reaches the final unconditional else (jsonio.ado:295) which calls printAllToFile.  metaprint() is not merely ignored -- the call silently degrades to a full data+metadata dump.

jsonio_display_formats.note: jsonio was read only.  Nothing in StataJSON was modified.

jsonio_value_boundary.finding: MEASURED, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE SECTION 08 OVERVIEW.  Section 08 opens with "a %td variable arrives as a raw Stata SIF integer".  It does not.  jsonio renders EVERY %t* variable through its display format and emits a JSON STRING (sp500 date arrives as "02jan2001", not 14977), while still reporting variableIsString=false for it.  Numeric display formats are NOT applied: %9.0fc and %9.2f come across as raw JSON numbers.  So the Python side must parse a formatted date STRING, not offset an integer -- and _load_data's existing pd.to_numeric(..., errors="coerce") will turn those strings into NaN.  Tasks 08-03 and 08-04 must be re-read against this.

missing_value_encoding.numeric_formats: the four-character STRING 'null' -- quoted, so it is NOT a JSON null

jsonio_value_boundary.sp500_probe_cmd: jsonio out date close, what(all) filenm(<path>) metaprint(varnames varlabels vallabs labelnames)

subsecond_precision.finding: jsonio renders %tc through the DEFAULT %tc picture, which stops at whole seconds, so the .123 millisecond component is destroyed in transit.  Sub-second precision cannot be recovered on the Python side from what jsonio emits.

jsonio_value_boundary.why: jsonio is the only route data takes from Stata into dash_render.py, so whatever it emits for a formatted variable is the actual input to _load_data.  This block records that, measured, rather than assuming a raw SIF integer arrives.

leap_seconds.finding: Leap-second data IS available.  %tC and %tc interpret the SAME integer as instants that differ by the accumulated leap seconds: the offset measured with Cofc() runs from 9.0s to 27.0s across the probed range, growing with time.  Treating %tC as %tc is therefore wrong by up to that many seconds and, per section 08, is acceptable only if documented.
leap_seconds.method: Cofc(t) maps a %tc instant to the %tC value for the SAME instant, so Cofc(t) - t is the accumulated leap-second offset in milliseconds.  The same integer is also displayed under both pictures to show the two formats disagree on what a given number means.

left_aligned_prefix.note: Task 08-03 must match the %t / %-t prefix case-sensitively.  These rows show Stata accepting the left-aligned variant of each date format.  The SAME integer 14977 is fed to all eight, so the resulting instants deliberately differ -- the point of these rows is that the %-t spelling parses, not what it means.

ty_is_the_year_itself.conclusion: CONFIRMED: display %ty 38 prints "38", not "1998".  %ty carries the year itself; adding 1960 is wrong.
ty_is_the_year_itself.why_it_matters: Offsetting a %ty value from 1960 -- the arithmetic that is correct for the other seven formats -- turns 1998 into 3958.  %ty must be used as-is.
